entries.title: Recover from mismatched JS and WASM
entries.diagnostic: Initialization rejects with an EngineError mentioning a missing WASM export (wasm.__wbindgen_add_to_stack_pointer is not a function in the pinned Chromium run). The editor phase is failed, ready is false and no localCommitted receipt is created.
entries.reproduce: Save Due Thursday through the real editor, close it, then open the same database in a fresh browser realm. The prepared transport serves a valid eight-byte empty WASM module at the engine URL. This models incompatible JS/WASM bodies, rather than a network outage.
entries.recover: Retain the database identity and checkpoint. Dispose the failed instance, restore the exact paired JS/WASM assets, and reopen in a fresh realm. A successfully instantiated but incompatible WASM body can poison the generated module cache; retrying within that same realm does not replace its exports. The test independently expects Due Thursday and no error. It never reseeds or deletes the saved database.

entries.title: Preserve unsupported schema and custom content
entries.diagnostic: A restore request with schema future.schema.v99 rejects with EngineError / EngineRejected: unsupported identity envelope. Unknown custom data instead has a source fallback: Future kickoff. A fallback does not authorize editing that custom type.
entries.reproduce: Use the structural-callout-v2 production packages. Save an inert future.team-callout envelope at dataVersion 7 and a demo.highlight mark at version 9 with an extra retain field. Attempt restore with a deliberately incompatible expected schema, then reopen with extensions absent.
entries.recover: Keep the original checkpoint and journal unmodified. Reopen with the matching original identity and compatible runtime. The test compares complete block structures before/after and restored serialization, the nested unknown payload, future mark version/extra field and visible fallback. Do not reconstruct a document from fallback text or silently downgrade its schema.

entries.title: Recover from cancelled browser initialization
entries.diagnostic: ready rejects with initialization canceled. A visible host element does not establish ready state. A cancelled instance reaches destroyed and releases subscriptions and recovered storage.
entries.reproduce: Save Due Thursday, close the editor, and hold the prepared recovery port while opening. Dispose before recovery resolves, then release the held real recovery. Await all issued sessions being disposed.
entries.recover: Keep the database and its identity. Dispose the cancelled editor and explicitly remount after late recovery has released its writer/storage resources. The independently expected result is Due Thursday with a live ready instance; final close releases it.

entries.title: Keep browser initialization behind the client boundary
entries.diagnostic: The deliberate null-host server-side mount reports Invalid value used in weak set in pinned Node 24.19.0. This low-level error means no valid browser host was provided; it is not a user-facing SDK diagnostic contract. Importing the public core/web entries alone accesses none of window, document, indexedDB, navigator, fetch or WebAssembly.
entries.reproduce: Run the pinned production tarballs in a Node child process with throwing getters for browser globals. Import core/web without mounting, then deliberately call createEditor with no browser host. The diagnostic is recorded separately from the import result.
entries.recover: Render a host on the server and mount only after browser hydration. The loading reproduction separately executes real browser mount, cancellation and remount with saved content. The qualified React/SSR and Astro static/SSR/navigation quickstarts provide the complete framework lifecycle; do not run createEditor during SSR.

entries.title: Recover an unsaved edit after quota failure
entries.diagnostic: QuotaExceededError: Prepared local quota failure. localCommitted is null for the failed edit, and the indicator does not claim Saved locally. Remote save remains not-configured.
entries.reproduce: Enable the prepared IndexedDB readwrite failure in the owning lifecycle consumer, replace Friday with Thursday, and await the rejected local flush. Assert Due Thursday remains visible before teardown.
entries.recover: Destroy with policy report and retain the returned recovery checkpoint and unsaved updates. The test requires nonempty bytes and updates, creates a distinct recovery database from the complete checkpoint, and independently reads Due Thursday with no error. Keep the original database and backup until recovery is verified. A production export must retain both checkpoint and journal bytes; do not save only rendered text.

entries.title: Handle revoked host write permission
entries.diagnostic: The captured intent returns rejected / stale-or-unavailable-command-target; new capture is unavailable and direct public commit throws Editor is read-only.
entries.reproduce: Select Friday in the command consumer, capture replace, then have the prepared host revoke write access using setReadOnly(true). Attempt both the old intent and a direct commit. Compare full block snapshots before/after.
entries.recover: Preserve the document and keep editing disabled until the authoritative host explicitly reauthorizes it. The fixture then calls setReadOnly(false), reselects Friday and captures a new replace command. Only that new intent commits Due Thursday. This is a local host-policy fixture, not a remote ACL service or OS permission test.

entries.title: Recover a stale command without retargeting
entries.diagnostic: The captured replace intent returns rejected / stale-or-unavailable-command-target after another admitted edit advances the revision.
entries.reproduce: Select Friday and capture replace. Apply Bold through the owning command consumer before executing the captured replacement with Monday. Compare complete semantic/selection snapshots around the rejected execution.
entries.recover: Discard and dispose the stale intent. Ask for or deliberately establish a new selection, then recapture replace. The old intent leaves Due Friday and all newer formatting intact; the new intent alone changes it to Due Thursday. Never retry against an implicit current caret.

scope: Prepared failures through exact local production runtime; no external release/platform qualification
